text:
Predicates:
HouseholdAppliance(x) ::: x is a household appliance.
Sucks(x) ::: x sucks.
Space :::
Vampire(x) ::: x is a vampire.
Vacuum(x) ::: x is a vacuum.
Plunger(x) ::: x is a plunger.
Duster(x) ::: x is a duster.
Question: ::: Is it true that if something is a household appliance, then it sucks?

Premises:
Plunger(x) ∧ Sucks(x) ::: Plungers suck.
Vacuums(x) ∧ Sucks(x) ::: Vacuums suck.
Vampire(x) ∧ Sucks(x) ::: Vampires suck.
Space :::
Vacuum(space) ::: Space is a vacuum.
Duster(x) ∧ ¬Sucks(x) ::: A duster does not suck.

Conclusion:
∀x (HouseholdAppliance(x) → Sucks(x)) ::: If something is a household appliance, then it sucks.
